grades.quote: Configure the spacing of exceptions and interrupt entries. When VS=0, all exceptions and interrupts have the same entry base address.
grades.reason: Describes the ECFG.VS configuration field, which sets whether all exceptions and interrupts share one entry base or are spaced apart. It also notes that TLB refill and machine error entries are separate. This is the configuration half of the answer, but it doesn't give the full address calculation.

grades.quote: All general exception entries have the same base address from `CSR.EENTRY` .
grades.reason: Directly answers the question. TLB refill and machine error exceptions use their own entry registers. General exceptions use the CSR.EENTRY base ORed with an offset derived from ecode and the ECFG.VS setting. It also explains the effect of VS=0 versus VS!=0.
Covers RISC-V RNMI cause and status registers (mncause, mnstatus). It does not say how a trap handler entry address is selected.

grades.quote: so the calculation of interrupt entries follows the rules for calculating general exception entries.
grades.reason: Explains that interrupt entries are calculated with the general exception entry rules. The exception number is the interrupt number plus 64. This is a useful partial answer for interrupts, but it relies on the Exception Entry section for the actual calculation.
